stage1.impression: A dark wood-lined bar with two big speakers in niches, two white pendants and a counter seen from a stool. It reads as a competent CG render, not a photograph. The pale squares of concrete behind the record shelves are the brightest and coolest thing in the frame and look like lit glass panels. The speakers are near-black boxes that sink into their niches, the pendants read as white enamel, the shelving is mostly empty, and a black chair back fills the lower middle. As a magazine picture it reads as a generic lounge, not a specific place: the altar-like niches and the Domes do not come through.

blocking_9: The niche speakers read at a glance as smoked cast acrylic with light passing through them (speaker regions lum_median >= 45, with visible glowing edges and the white batts showing through the tint)
The concrete behind the record wall sits below the speakers in brightness, warm under 2400 K (r_median > b_median), with board-form grain and tie holes that do not repeat cubby to cubby
The record wall is full of records, so it reads as a working listening bar and not an empty display shelf
The Domes read as tinted smoked acrylic with a softly glowing liner, not white enamel shades
The foreground no longer has a crushed black chair back as its largest shape; the lower third holds detail
Visible atmosphere and distinct pools of light on the zinc under each Dome, with dark falling off between them
The materials hold up at 1:1: fluted oak with real grain variation, zinc with patina, and nothing that looks smooth CG or tiled

defects.what: Left niche speaker is underlit (median 24): it reads as a black box with a woofer and gives no sense of acrylic or tint
Right niche speaker is underlit (median 36) and half hidden behind the pendant and its shadow
Concrete in the record-wall cubbies is cool (R150 G153 B156) and bright (lum 152) under 2400 K light, so it reads as a back-lit frosted panel
The same tie-hole blemish appears in the same place in every concrete cubby, which reads as tiling
The record wall is mostly empty, with only a few clumps of records, so it looks like a showroom shelf
Dome pendant reads as an opaque white enamel shade: no smoked tint and no depth in the acrylic
Second Dome is the same, white and flat
The foreground chair back is a crushed black void (73% crushed) taking up the lower centre
The zinc counter's front edge has a long, even, hot specular streak that reads as CG
The fluted oak front is smooth and even, with grain that looks repeated, and it carries no light pool
The request column's coins show saturated reds and blues; they compete with the speakers for the frame's only colour
No visible atmosphere and no defined pools on the bar top: the light reads as an even low wash, not practicals

changes.problem: The niche speakers are the heroes but sit below the frame's median and read as black boxes.

change.setting: the lit niche's strip and the light plinths under the niche speakers (plus a small narrow spot per niche raking the cabinet front)
change.to: strip 14.0; add 1 x spot per niche, 15 W, 2700 K, cone 18 deg, aimed down the cabinet face from the niche head

changes.expected: Light through the smoked acrylic from below and its edges glowing; the white batts show faintly through the tint; both speakers become the brightest non-lamp objects after the bar top

changes.problem: The concrete behind the record wall is the coolest and brightest surface in the frame and reads as glowing glass, which pulls the eye off the speakers.

change.setting: the concrete's tone and sheen (record-wall back)
change.from: light, cool grey, one repeated blemish map
change.to: albedo down about 40% to a warm mid-grey (about #7A736B), matte, with a board-form grain and tie-hole map in world space and a random offset per cubby

changes.expected: Concrete reads as a warm, receding backdrop under the lamps, darker than the speakers, with no repeat

changes.problem: The record wall is mostly empty cubbies, so the room reads as a showroom and not a listening bar.

evidence.measured: about 12 of 16 visible cubbies show bare concrete; records in only about 4

change.setting: props: records in the record wall
change.to: fill about 85% of cubbies with LP spines (varied, worn, mostly black and brown with a few pale spines), a couple face-out sleeves in neutral tones, one or two leaning gaps

changes.expected: A dense, lived-in wall of small spine highlights; the concrete shows only in slivers; lum of the wall drops toward 50-70

changes.problem: The Domes read as white enamel shades because the liner's glow overpowers the smoked tint.

evidence.measured: lum_median 152, near-neutral RGB 161/150/143; no tint gradient across the shade

change.setting: EARF's lamps: each Dome's liner glow
change.to: 0.12 (keep 30 W downlight output; raise the Domes' downlights to compensate on the zinc if needed)

changes.expected: The shade reads as dark smoked acrylic with a glowing inner liner at the rim, and a bright opening underneath

changes.problem: The foreground chair back is a black void that takes the lower centre, and the fluted front gets a third of the frame.

change.to: position [6.0, 2.9, 1.25] (move behind the chair line, off the chair back), target [7.1, 6.0, 1.42]

changes.expected: The chair back leaves the frame or becomes an edge silhouette; the counter sits on the lower third; the niches and Domes gain height

changes.problem: The light is an even low wash, with no visible pools under the Domes and no atmosphere.

evidence.measured: bar-top band lum_median 40, with the light spread evenly across it; haze 0.01

change.setting: haze density and the Domes' downlights
change.to: haze 0.03; downlights 180 W, cone 16 deg, so each lands a distinct pool on the zinc

changes.expected: Two defined pools on the counter, with darker zinc between them and a faint visible cone under each Dome

changes.problem: The zinc's front edge carries a long, even specular streak that reads as CG.

evidence.measured: band clip 0.18%, p95 171, one continuous bright line

change.to: roughness about 0.35, with a mottled patina map and wipe marks so the highlight breaks up

changes.expected: A soft, broken sheen along the edge, brightest only under the Domes

changes.problem: The fluted oak front is uniform, with repeating grain, and it reads as a CG surface at 1:1.

change.from: uniform dark stain, one grain texture
change.to: per-flute random grain offset and slight tone variation (about 8%), a little sheen on the flute crowns, and edge wear at knee height

changes.expected: The flutes read as solid timber, and their crowns catch spill from the counter

out_of_scope.request: A lighter or less smoked tint on the niche speakers so they read as the colour accent
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' colour is fixed by the Smoke configuration; only the light through them may change

out_of_scope.request: Mute the saturated coin colours in the request column
out_of_scope.why: The EARFcoins are EARF's product in the configuration; if their colours are not meant to be part of Smoke, the owner has to decide that

out_of_scope.request: Pull the right niche speaker out from behind the pendant
out_of_scope.why: The niche positions and the Dome positions are fixed by the room's design; only the camera may resolve the overlap
